direct_evidence: Hidden Hand grows by making itself useful to authorities; benefits patrons by attacking commercial rivals; also uses brigandage, enforcement and stolen-goods trade.
authority_relation: Functional interface with authorities is described, but formal authorization is not stated.
comparative_value: Tests state use/tolerance of non-state coercion and patronage.
localization_status: Official faction name: 秘密之手; matching CN key present.
limits: No command chain, legal immunity or prevalence data.

direct_evidence: Frontier knowledge brings imperial commanders' attention; leaders receive titles; young men enter archons' and emperors' retinues.
authority_relation: Selective incorporation; the group remains hostile to actual imperial authority.
coercion_or_resource: Military service is implied, not fully specified.
comparative_value: Tests whether incorporation yields obedience or political integration.
localization_status: Faction name: 自由民; CN description renders retinues as 私兵; English wording is retained in analysis.
limits: No legal process, scale or full institutional status.

direct_evidence: Bureau of Barbarian Affairs asks for patient information and later threatens disclosure of doctor-patient relations to compel a confession.
authority_relation: Formal institution directly exerts coercion through information and professional reputation.
comparative_value: Counterexample to the idea that coercion is only outside the state.
localization_status: CN keys present; institution rendered 蛮族事务局.
limits: Single character account; no administrative orders or judicial records.

direct_evidence: Leonipardes reportedly arbitrate only when both parties invite them; judgments are obeyed; livestock rustling and blood feuds are common.
authority_relation: Local arbitration depends on invitation and acceptance, not routine central intervention.
coercion_or_resource: Disputes include livestock rustling and blood feuds; arbitration is conditional.
comparative_value: Tests procedural legitimacy and local autonomy.
localization_status: CN place name 波罗斯 appears in encyclopedia; key absent from attached std_settlements CN table; compiled Chinese text shifts the crime description.
limits: Rumor marker it is said; no case records; Chinese source chain unresolved.

direct_evidence: Brotherhood of the Woods begins as a peasant movement and later uses extortion, terror and corrupt deals with local authorities.
authority_relation: Rebel organization enters coercive extraction and corrupt local bargains.
coercion_or_resource: Extortion and terror; food supply and anti-informant control are cited as pressures.
comparative_value: Tests organizational survival and legitimacy erosion.
localization_status: Official name: 绿林兄弟会; CN key present.
limits: Faction overview; not every member or period.

direct_evidence: Independent peasantry and heterodox ideas are noted; nobles sometimes fund rebellions to use against rival Vlandian houses.
authority_relation: Elite patronage can shape rebellion; not purely bottom-up mobilization.
coercion_or_resource: Rebellion supported at times by aristocratic funding.
comparative_value: Strong alternative to a single-cause account of rebel coercive drift.
localization_status: CN place name 杰屈朗 appears in encyclopedia; key absent from attached std_settlements CN table.
limits: No funding contracts or event dates; source chain for Chinese text unresolved.

direct_evidence: Alley protectors gain respect from residents; a guard captain asks one to cover an abduction and provide information; he refuses and leaves.
authority_relation: Community legitimacy conflicts with official demands.
coercion_or_resource: Pressure, threats to family, demands to conceal abuse and supply intelligence.
comparative_value: Cross-cultural test of trust, official office and local intermediaries.
localization_status: Protector is translated as 守护者 in CN language table.
limits: Single character narrative; not direct evidence for Imperial institutions.

direct_evidence: Beni Zilal / Sons of the Shadows collect protection money from caravans and make deals with local potentates.
authority_relation: Non-state group combines route control, coercive collection and elite bargains.
coercion_or_resource: Protection money and threat of assassination in origin legend.
comparative_value: Compares protection economies without equating them to Hidden Hand.
localization_status: Official faction name: 暗影之子; CN key present.
limits: Origins explicitly legendary; no proof of public acceptance.

direct_evidence: Forest People use slash-and-burn farming outside the grasp of Sturgian boyars; plots are hard to measure and tax.
authority_relation: Livelihood and spatial dispersion limit lordly control.
coercion_or_resource: Tax measurement and governance avoidance are explicit; no organized armed resistance described.
comparative_value: Tests autonomy through production and land measurability rather than formal law alone.
localization_status: Official faction name: 森民; CN key present.
limits: Faction overview; no population or tax totals.

direct_evidence: A fence dispute leads to killing; cousins intend to take the narrator to judgment; he offers blood-money but kills two more and flees unable to pay for three.
authority_relation: Kinship adjudication and compensation can constrain violence but may be overwhelmed by escalation.
coercion_or_resource: Homicide, threatened judgment, blood-money and retaliatory killings.
comparative_value: Tests customary settlement and its failure under escalation.
localization_status: CN text varies between 血债 and 赔偿款/赔偿金.
limits: Narrator is self-justifying; not a codified legal record.

direct_evidence: Urkhunid khans offer farmland and serfs in exchange for taxes and military levies; the nomadic clan resists settling.
authority_relation: State attempts to exchange land and dependent labor for fiscal and military obligations; clan resists but still trades and intermaries with settled groups.
coercion_or_resource: Kidnapping for ransom and flock-raiding are also described.
comparative_value: Tests settlement, taxation, levy and political compliance as a contested exchange.
localization_status: Faction id karakhuzaits has display name Karakhergit, localized 喀拉库吉特.
limits: Faction narrative is evaluative; not all Khuzait clans behave alike.

direct_evidence: A peddler's son says steppe tribes look down on tax-paying villagers, trample crops and take people to war; he seeks refuge among a clan that does not answer to the khan.
authority_relation: Tax and military extraction are experienced as coercive by one villager; alternative belonging is sought among fugitives' hosts.
coercion_or_resource: Crop destruction and forced recruitment as described by narrator.
comparative_value: Tests how the same political order is experienced differently by villagers and steppe groups.
localization_status: Dialogue renders Karakhuzaits as 喀拉库赛特, while faction display name is 喀拉库吉特; do not silently normalize.
limits: Personal grievance, not neutral tax or recruitment register.
